Creality launches SPARKX i7 Nano: bringing compact multi-color printing to €299.

Aug 15, 2026, 10:17 ET

FRANKFURT, Germany, Aug. 15, 2026 /PRNewswire/ - Creality, a global leader in the 3D printing industry, announced the availability of the SPARKX i7 Nano, the latest addition to its i7 series. This desktop 3D printer saves space while delivering premium print quality across up to four colors. With a minimalist design that fits easily on a desk, the i7 Nano makes multi-color 3D printing more compact, affordable, and accessible.

Following the January debut of the i7 Color Combo, the i7 Nano is also built for smarter, more effortless 3D printing. It integrates AI-powered capabilities that simplify both creation and printing, including CubeMe for automatically turning 2D portraits into multi-color 3D models. A built-in 720p AI camera monitors prints for common failures such as spaghetti and air printing, while vibration compensation and dynamic pressure adjustment help maintain consistent print quality.

Beyond these shared features, the i7 Nano comes with an integrated spool holder and optimized filament layout, taking up less desktop space and making it easier to fit into compact workspaces. The spool holder mounts directly onto the printer body with a convenient snap-on design, eliminating the need for an external CFS Lite. This compact solution keeps the printer's footprint small while maintaining a clean appearance without compromising printing performance.

Paired with the new CFS nano Kit, a small unit mounted on top of the printer, the i7 Nano enables vibrant multi-color printing with automatic filament switching for up to four colors. The CFS nano features a dual-motor system, with one motor controlling filament channel switching and the other handling filament feeding and retraction. This ensures smooth and efficient color changes while keeping the overall setup streamlined. The CFS nano also allows quick installation without complex disassembly or modifications and is compatible with existing i7 units.

The i7 Nano features a build volume of 260 x 260 x 255 mm and a maximum printing speed of up to 500 mm/s. It supports a hardened steel nozzle with a maximum temperature of 300°C and multiple nozzle diameters, including 0.2, 0.4, 0.6, and 0.8 mm. It is also equipped with automatic bed leveling, RFID filament reading and automatic filament refill to deliver an easy-to-use and reliable printing experience for beginners.

The SPARKX i7 Nano with CFS nano Kit will be available starting from August 15 for €299 in Europe at the Creality EU Store.

Discover Creality: the ultimate guide to a leading 3D printer manufacturer.

In the rapidly evolving world of additive manufacturing, Creality stands out as a powerhouse, making high-quality 3D printing accessible to hobbyists, educators, professionals, and businesses alike. Founded in 2014, Creality has grown from a small workshop in Shenzhen, China, into a global leader, shipping millions of units worldwide and fostering a vibrant community of creators. This comprehensive guide dives deep into Creality's history, product lineup, innovations, and why it's a top choice for anyone searching for the best 3D printers, laser engravers, 3D scanners, filaments, resins, and more. Whether you're a beginner exploring affordable 3D printers or a pro seeking advanced features like high-speed printing, Creality offers solutions that balance performance, affordability, and reliability.

Creality's origins: from humble beginnings to global dominance.

Creality's story is one of passion and perseverance. In 2014, four young innovators - Jack Chen (Chen Chun), Adun Ao (Ao Danjun), Fred Liu (Liu Huilin), and Michael Tang (Tang Jingke) - met at a 3D printing exhibition and decided to democratize the technology. Starting in a modest workshop, they focused on creating user-friendly, affordable 3D printers. Their first model, the CR-3, marked the beginning of a journey that has seen the company expand to over 550 employees, with offices in Beijing, Shanghai, Wuhan, Huizhou, and beyond. Today, headquartered in Shenzhen, Creality operates in more than 100 countries, producing over 500,000 units annually and holding dozens of patents.

The name "Creality" embodies their mission: blending creativity with reality through 3D printing. Over the past decade, they've diversified beyond printers into a full ecosystem, including filaments, resins, scanners, engravers, and software. This growth is fueled by a commitment to innovation, as evidenced by their R&D investments in FDM (Fused Deposition Modeling), resin (SLA/DLP), and hybrid technologies. Creality's success is also reflected in community-driven events like ShareFest, where users showcase prints and collaborate, reinforcing their slogan: "Imagine It, Make It."

Creality 3D: Company History and Review of the Current Lineup | Top 3D Shop

By 2024, celebrating their 10th anniversary, Creality had launched groundbreaking products like the K1 series, emphasizing speed and AI integration. Their evolution from DIY kits to fully assembled, professional-grade machines has made them a staple in homes, schools, and workshops globally.

Creality's extensive product lineup: something for every creator.

Creality's portfolio is vast, covering everything from entry-level 3D printers for beginners to advanced tools for industrial applications. Let's break it down by category, highlighting key features, models, and how they add value.

3D printers: FDM and resin options for all levels.

Creality is synonymous with FDM 3D printers, which use thermoplastic filaments to build objects layer by layer. Their flagship Ender series has sold millions, praised for ease of assembly and upgradability.

* Ender Series: Ideal for beginners, the Ender-3 V3 KE offers a 220x220x240mm build volume, auto-leveling, and speeds up to 500mm/s. Upgrades like the Ender-3 V3 Plus include larger builds (300x300x330mm) and CoreXZ mechanics for stability. These printers support PLA, ABS, TPU, and more, making them perfect for prototypes, toys, and custom parts. Reviews highlight their quiet operation and open-source compatibility, allowing endless modifications.

Creality 3D Ender 3 Pro Review | Tested & Rated

* K1 Series: For high-speed enthusiasts, the K1 Max boasts a 300x300x300mm enclosed build area, AI camera for monitoring, and speeds up to 600mm/s. It handles advanced filaments like carbon fiber-infused materials, ideal for engineering and cosplay. The K1C variant adds multi-color printing via AMS (Automatic Material System), enhancing creativity without manual swaps.

Creality3D K1 Max large high speed 3D printer.

* Other FDM Lines: The CR series, like CR-10 Smart Pro, offers massive builds (300x300x400mm) with Wi-Fi connectivity and auto-bed leveling. For education, the Sermoon D3 provides enclosed safety features. Creality also ventures into hybrid machines like the CP-01, combining 3D printing, laser engraving, and CNC milling.

Shifting to resin 3D printers, Creality excels in SLA/DLP technology for high-detail prints. The HALOT-MAGE series features 10.3-inch LCD screens for resolutions down to 0.05mm, perfect for jewelry, miniatures, and dental models. Models like the HALOT-MAGE Pro include air purifiers and smart resin pumps for safer, easier use. With powerful chips and optimized slicing software, these printers minimize failures and support complex geometries.

Creality's 3D printers start at around $200 for basic models, scaling to $1,000+ for pros, offering exceptional value compared to competitors.

Laser engravers: precision cutting and engraving.

Expanding beyond printing, Creality's laser engravers like the Falcon series bring versatility to makers. The Falcon2 22W uses diode lasers for engraving wood, leather, acrylic, and even cutting thin metals. Features include air assist for clean cuts, offline operation, and compatibility with LightBurn software. Higher-power options like the Falcon2 40W handle thicker materials, making them ideal for custom signs, jewelry, and prototyping.

The CV-01 adds portability with a compact design, while the CP-01 integrates engraving into a multi-function device. These engravers emphasize safety with enclosed frames and exhaust systems, appealing to hobbyists and small businesses searching for affordable laser engravers.

3D scanners: capturing reality in detail.

Creality's 3D scanners bridge the physical and digital worlds. The CR-Scan Lizard offers 0.05mm accuracy for small objects, using structured light for quick scans. For larger items, the CR-Scan Ferret Pro provides handheld mobility with anti-shake tech and color mapping. Professional-grade options like the CR-Scan Raptor deliver sub-millimeter precision for reverse engineering, art restoration, and medical applications.

These scanners integrate seamlessly with Creality software, allowing users to scan, edit, and print in one workflow. Priced from $300 to $1,000, they're accessible yet powerful, supporting formats like OBJ and STL.

Filaments, resins, and accessories: fueling your prints.

No 3D printing ecosystem is complete without materials. Creality's filaments include Hyper PLA for high-speed printing (up to 600mm/s without jamming), available in colors and types like matte, silk, and carbon fiber. Their Ender PLA is budget-friendly, eco-conscious, and tangle-free.

For resin printing, Creality offers standard, water-washable, and tough resins in various colors, curing quickly under UV light for smooth finishes. Accessories like nozzles, build plates, enclosures, and dry boxes (e.g., SpacePi X4) enhance durability and print quality.

Resin vs Filaments for 3D Printing - Which One is Better for You?

Creality Cloud and slicers like Creality Print provide cloud-based monitoring, model libraries, and AI-optimized settings, rounding out the ecosystem.

Innovations driving Creality's success.

Creality's edge lies in relentless innovation. They've pioneered high-speed FDM with CoreXY and Klipper firmware, reducing print times dramatically. AI features in the K1 series include failure detection and time-lapse videos. Sustainability efforts include biodegradable filaments, while open-source roots encourage community mods.

Recent launches like the SparkX i7 emphasize multi-material printing and larger builds. Their R&D spans STEAM education tools, drones, and robots, positioning Creality at the forefront of additive manufacturing trends.

Building a thriving Community and support network.

Creality isn't just about products; it's about people. With millions of users, their community thrives on forums, YouTube (hundreds of thousands of views per review), and events like the 2024 ShareFest in Chicago, where creators share tips and win prizes.

Support includes a robust wiki, online chat, 1-year warranties, and 14-day returns. Creality Cloud connects users for collaborative projects, fostering innovation in education, art, and industry.

Creality ShareFest 2024: Another Celebration of Community and Inspiration in Chicago

Why choose Creality? Value, quality, and versatility.

Creality delivers unmatched value: High-performance machines at competitive prices, backed by a global supply chain. Users rave about reliability - printers like the Ender-3 often outlast expectations with minimal maintenance. For businesses, scalability from prototypes to production is seamless.

Compared to brands like Prusa or Anycubic, Creality offers broader ecosystems and faster innovation. Whether for 3D printing hobbyists, educators teaching STEM, or pros in design, Creality empowers turning ideas into tangible realities.

Conclusion: join the Creality revolution today.

Creality has transformed 3D printing from niche tech to everyday tool, with a decade of growth showing no signs of slowing. From the iconic Ender series to cutting-edge scanners and engravers, their products inspire creativity worldwide. Explore Creality's full range on its site - whether you're buying your first 3D printer or upgrading to high-speed models. Start creating today and experience why millions trust Creality to "Create and Think 3D."

Orbbec and Creality launch Pika, bringing 3D scanning into the pocket era.

June 2, 2026

Creality unveiled Pika, a next-generation AI-powered portable 3D scanner co-developed with Orbbec, during its 12th Anniversary "AI Ecosystem" product launch event.

Powered by Orbbec's core underlying technologies, Pika breaks the mold of traditional 3D scanners by combining high-precision scanning, intelligent AI computing, and an ultra-portable design into one compact device. This launch marks a significant leap forward in integrated hardware and software innovation for the 3D scanning industry.

Orbbec and Creality deepen strategic partnership.

Creality, the global consumer 3D printing ecosystem leader, officially debuted on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange. On the same day, Orbbec and Creality announced a deepened strategic partnership, including the establishment of a "3D Scanner Digital Joint Innovation Center" and the joint development of a next-generation "3D Printing AI Vision Intelligent Platform".

Built upon technological innovation and ecosystem collaboration, the partnership aims to accelerate the high-quality development of the 3D printing industry, empowering creators and digital manufacturing enterprises worldwide.

Against this backdrop of strategic collaboration and AI-driven innovation, the two companies officially unveiled Pika during Creality's 12th Anniversary "AI Ecosystem" product launch event - a next-generation AI-powered portable 3D scanner co-developed by Orbbec and Creality.

Ultra-Portable design for 3D scanning.

One of Pika's most significant innovations is its highly compact form factor, bringing truly portable 3D scanning into daily creative workflows.

Measuring just 100 x 60 x 35 mm and weighing a mere 260 g, Pika is pocket-sized and engineered for mobility. The device can operate directly with a smartphone - no PC required - unlocking unprecedented freedom for outdoor scanning and mobile content production.

Compared with conventional bulky scanning systems, Pika offers a user experience on pair with modern consumer electronics.

The device also features a built-in HD display for real-time scanning previews and a quick-release replaceable battery for uninterrupted mobile operations.

With the point-and-shoot simplicity of smartphone photography, Pika significantly lowers the technical threshold for professional-grade 3D scanning. Creators, designers, engineers, and hobbyists alike can now capture high-quality scans anytime and anywhere.

High-Speed scanning with up to 110 FPS performance.

Pika is designed to deliver a faster, more stable, and more reliable portable scanning experience.

Built on a global shutter 3D camera architecture, Pika could inherently eliminate motion blur during handheld operation. Compared with conventional rolling-shutter systems that frequently suffer from ghosting, distortion, or loss of tracking during movement, Pika maintains stable and clear data capture while scanning in motion.

Pika also delivers industry-leading high-frame-rate performance. In smartphone mode, line-laser scanning supports up to 40 FPS, while infrared mode reaches up to 20 FPS. When connected to a PC, line-laser scanning can achieve up to 110 FPS, significantly improving scanning efficiency and reducing tracking interruptions.

This high frame rate not only enables faster scanning, but also provides smoother and more stable data acquisition across diverse scenarios - from object scanning and full-body capture to complex structural modeling.

One device for diverse creative applications.

Pika integrates both 7-line blue laser and infrared structured light technologies, enabling both ultra-fine and high-speed scanning within a single device.

The blue laser system delivers scanning accuracy of up to 0.03 mm, allowing precise capture of fine textures and intricate geometric details. It is particularly suitable for high-precision applications such as mechanical components, collectible figures, and cultural artifacts.

Meanwhile, the infrared structured light mode is optimized for human-body scanning, large-object capture, and marker-free scanning workflows.

Beyond hardware, Pika also incorporates advanced AI-powered algorithms for more stable target tracking, smarter data processing, and streamlined scanning workflows. Even first-time users can quickly generate high-quality 3D models for digital creation and 3D printing applications.

Besides, Pika's AI-powered body completion algorithm also simplifies portrait 3D printing by automatically generating complete printable models with virtually zero manual editing.

Bringing 3D scanning to the masses.

Since forging their strategic partnership in 2023, Orbbec and Creality have collaborated on multiple 3D scanning and smart manufacturing products powered by Orbbec's core technologies.

As a leading provider of robotics and AI vision technology, Orbbec remains committed to advancing high-performance and accessible 3D imaging solutions through continuous innovation in sensors, AI vision, and integrated hardware-software systems.

Moving forward, Orbbec will continue working with Creality to accelerate the adoption of AI-powered digital creation technologies, empowering creators, makers, designers, and businesses worldwide.

Creality announces KliTek 3D printer nozzle changing.

If you buy something through its links, ToolGuyd might earn an affiliate commission.

Discover more

Electrical Tools

Screwdriver

Creality has announced KliTek, "next-gen nozzle changing" 3D Printing technology.

They're calling this a "game changer" and say that KliTek will allow for multicolor and multi-material 3D printing "in a brand-new fashion."

"Print faster without waste and hassle-free in one go."

This seems like more of a teaser, with little details. But, there's enough to get a small sense of what Creality is going for here.

They say "speed isn't the point" and that "getting the model done faster is." "it's about one-and-done vibrancy."

Similarly, "multi-material itself isn't the point - it's about possibilities, like merging the rigid with the flexible."

An image notes that you can use a 0.4mm nozzle for outer wall details and 0.8mm for faster infills.

To my knowledge, you cannot mix nozzle sizes in competing brands' multi-nozzle or tool-head systems, only colors or materials.

As far as technical details are concerned, it sounds like Creality is just swapping out the hot end and nozzle, rather than the entire toolhead.

The modularity Toolguyd achieved hit a sweet spot - the nozzle assembly weighs just one-fifth of the weight of the full toolhead. It's a 5-second nozzle change.

They also added a second extruder for a pull-push configuration, to help softer TPU filaments perform more reliably. "It moves through the tube like a caterpillar."

Creality KliTek is "coming 2026."

The company has also been talking about an "AI Ecosystem."

But it's not exactly clear what the "AI Ecosystem" will involve with respect to their 3D printers, slicers, or control software.

Other nozzle-changing 3D printers.

Several nozzle-changing 3D printers have emerged in the past year. Some swap just the nozzle and hothead, and others swap the entire toolhead.

The Snapmaker U1 has a toolhead changer that swaps between 4 complete toolheads.

The Bambu H2C has 2 extruders, one that's fixed and the other that can swap between 6 induction-heated hotend nozzle assemblies.

Prusa has the Core One+ 3D printer and recently launched INDX 4- and 8-nozzle toolhead changing system. Prusa claims their upgraded system is for multicolor and "true multi-material" 3D printing with "virtually zero waste."

Creality unveils "desktop Micro-Factory" Ecosystem at RAPID+TCT 2026, redefining professional manufacturing for the masses.

April 22, 2026 at 18:19 PM EDT

i This article is third-party content and does not represent the views of this site. We make no guarantees regarding its accuracy or completeness.

BOSTON - April 22, 2026 - Creality, a global leader in 3D printing technology, made a significant impact at the RAPID+TCT 2026 exhibition in Boston, showcasing a comprehensive vision of the future: the "Desktop Micro-Factory." By integrating AI-driven hardware, a cross-process ecosystem, and a sustainable recycling loop, Creality is transitioning 3D printing from a niche hobbyist tool into an accessible, professional-grade appliance for studios, schools, and small businesses.

The centerpiece of the Creality booth was the R1 Shredder and M1 Filament Generator. This innovative recycling system, which launched on Indiegogo in late March, achieved a staggering 10 million RMB (approx. $1.4M USD) within its first 20 minutes and surpassed 30 million RMB on its first day.

The R1/M1 system addresses a critical industry pain point: material waste. With an output of 1kg per hour, the system allows users to recycle failed prints and support structures back into high-quality filament. "This is a game-changer for my studio," noted a visitor at the event. "It's not just about saving money; it's about creating a sustainable, closed-loop printing environment."

"Appliancification": Lowering the Barrier to Entry with AI

Creality's new SPARKX i7 3D printer demonstrated the industry's shift toward "appliancification" - making high-tech tools as easy to use as home appliances. Featuring AI machine vision for real-time error detection and a "5-second quick-swap" nozzle design, the SPARKX i7 removes the steep learning curve traditionally associated with 3D printing.

Complementing the hardware, Creality Cloud showcased its latest AI Modeling tools. Users can now generate complex 3D models - from personalized figurines to relief art - simply by uploading a photo via a smartphone app, bypassing the need for complex CAD modeling skills.

The "Desktop Micro-Factory" Ecosystem

Unlike competitors limited to a single product line, Creality's "Desktop Micro-Factory" encompasses a full production lifecycle:

* Digital Input: The Sermoon P1 3D scanner provides high-precision, wireless digitization of physical objects, even capturing difficult black or metallic surfaces without the need for scanning sprays.
* Multi-Material Manufacturing: The Falcon T1, the world's first 5-in-1 laser engraver, features swappable light modules to process wood, acrylic, metal, and glass.
* Precision Output: The HALOT X1 resin printer provides professional-grade detail with an automated resin management system, integrating seamlessly into the desktop workflow.

Commercial Viability and Market Outlook

The practical application of this ecosystem was vividly displayed through a collection of custom 3D-printed footwear at the booth, which drew significant interest for on-demand manufacturing and retail customization.

By bridging the gap between "3D Scanning - AI Modeling - Multi-process Manufacturing - Waste Recycling," Creality is providing a blueprint for decentralized, low-cost commercial production. As technology moves away from its "hardcore" technical labels, Creality is leading the charge toward a future where anyone can turn an idea into a physical product with the click of a button.

About Creality

Creality is a global pioneer in the 3D printing industry, dedicated to the democratization of 3D printing technology. With a product portfolio spanning FDM, Resin, 3D Scanners, and Laser Engravers, Creality provides end-to-end solutions for creators, professionals, and enterprises worldwide.

Sovol 3D printer teaser suggests large-format multi-color printing system.

- April 10, 2026

Why it matters.

Multi-color capability expands Sovol's market reach and meets rising demand for complex parts, while a low-waste system can cut material costs and boost efficiency for makers and small manufacturers.

Key takeaways.

* - Six visible spools imply a six-color printing system
* - Additional tube may support a dedicated TPU toolhead
* - Estimated build volume around 300-350 mm per side
* - Architecture hints at low-waste multi-extruder or tool-changer
* - Launch will keep Sovol competitive with Bambu, Prusa, Creality

Pulse analysis.

The desktop fused-filament fabrication (FFF) market has accelerated its shift toward multicolour capability, a feature once reserved for industrial machines. Brands such as Bambu Lab, Prusa Research, Anycubic, Creality and Snapmaker have already introduced printers that can blend up to six or more hues in a single print, unlocking new design possibilities for prototyping, education and small-batch production. Sovol, known for affordable, reliable printers, entered the conversation with a cryptic silhouette that reveals six external spools and a seventh filament inlet, hinting at a next-generation offering.

The visual clues point to a printer that can handle at least six colours, with the extra tube possibly dedicated to thermoplastic polyurethane (TPU), a flexible filament that challenges conventional swapping mechanisms. By routing each filament through its own feed, Sovol may be adopting a low-waste architecture similar to Vortek's hot-end swapping or INDX's multi-extruder layout, which dramatically reduces purge material and shortens changeover times. If the chassis indeed supports a 300-350 mm cubic build volume, it would compete directly with Bambu's H2D and other large-format workhorses.

Should Sovol confirm these specifications, the printer could attract hobbyists and small manufacturers seeking colour-rich parts without the waste penalties of traditional filament swapping. Lower material loss translates into cost savings, an appealing proposition for education labs and low-volume production lines where budget constraints are tight. Moreover, expanding its portfolio into high-end multicolour machines would reinforce Sovol's brand equity and diversify revenue streams, positioning the company as a viable alternative to the current market leaders. The upcoming launch will therefore be a litmus test for Sovol's ability to innovate and scale.

Kerry Stevenson

[Source: Sovol]

Sovol could be the next company to release a multimaterial desktop 3D printer.

The company has produced desktop equipment for many years and often provides "hints" of upcoming releases. This time, they've published a silhouette rendering of a new system, saying, "The Next Chapter is Coming."

In the promo post on X, they write:

"Something new is taking shape.

Out of the shadows, a new era of colour is coming.

Multi-filament. Multi-colour. And unmistakably Sovol.

Not ready to show you everything.

But ready to give you a first glimpse.

Stay tuned. The wait will be worth it."

This is not so surprising, as their main competitors - Bambu Lab, Prusa Research, Anycubic, Creality, and Snapmaker - have all released various forms of multicolour 3D printers. Sovol will have to do so to keep up.

However, there are two forms of multicolour FFF 3-D printing now on the scene:

* Traditional push-and-pull filament swapping into a single extruder
* More advanced systems that dramatically reduce purge waste (e.g., INDX, Vortek).

Which approach could Sovol be using?

What can PULSE learn about this development in advance of the official release?

All PULSE has to go on is the mysterious photo. Let's take a look at it in more depth to see what PULSE can determine.

Image analysis.

Image 2: Enhanced version of Sovol's mystery machine image

[Source: Fabbaloo]

* Six spools of filament are mounted externally in two rows of three spools, with six tube/port attachments on the top of the machine. This strongly suggests a six-colour system.
* The machine appears quite large. If those spools are standard 1 kg items, the printer likely has a large build volume - at least as tall as a Bambu Lab H2D, possibly 300 x 300 x 300 mm or larger (perhaps 350 x 350 x 350 mm).
* In addition to the six filament tubes, there is one more tube entering the machine at a different port. It looks identical to the others, so it is probably another filament feed.

* This could be for a separate toolhead dedicated to printing TPU, which is challenging for filament-swapping systems because TPU bends. Bambu Lab's H2D uses a separate toolhead and input port, and Sovol might be doing the same.
* If so, the machine could be a seven-colour system: six primary colours plus the secondary TPU filament.
* The spools appear mounted without an enclosure, suggesting there is no built-in drying capability. Competitors typically include drying, so it's unclear whether the visible spools are part of the final design or simply a visual cue to indicate a six-colour system. The "real" filament storage unit might be hidden.
* Regarding waste reduction, the image shows the filaments entering the unit separately at the top, unlike a traditional filament swapper that uses a single tube feeding one toolhead. This hints that Sovol may be employing a different architecture:

* Tool-changer with separate extruders for each filament (possible, though the spacing looks tight).
* Low-waste system similar to Vortek or INDX, where hot-ends are swapped, which could also explain the tight spacing.

Conclusion.

That's about all that can be derived from the mysterious image of Sovol's upcoming system. PULSE'll have to wait for the company to release more details, and they haven't indicated when that will happen.
attributes.title: Sovol 3D printer teaser suggests large-format multi-color printing system.

Creality Sermoon P1 redefines what a professional 3D scanner can be.

Mar 03, 2026, 06:51 ET

HONG KONG, March 3, 2026 /PRNewswire/ - Creality today announced the global availability of Sermoon P1, a professional handheld 3D scanner designed to deliver industrial-grade capabilities at an accessible price.

By combining true standalone operation with advanced multi-mode laser scanning, Sermoon P1 sets a new benchmark for what professionals can expect from a handheld 3D scanner.

Sermoon P1 is now available worldwide.

For years, professional 3D scanning has required expensive hardware, complex workflows, and powerful external computers. Sermoon P1 changes that by bringing advanced scanning performance into a more compact, efficient, and affordable form - built for engineers, automotive workshops, and professional studios.

True Standalone Performance for Professional Workflows

Sermoon P1 is a true standalone professional 3D scanner, powered by a Qualcomm 8-core processor, 24GB RAM, and 256GB high-speed storage.

Scanning, data processing, and model preview are performed directly on the device via a 6-inch HD touchscreen, eliminating the need for a high-end PC and significantly simplifying daily professional workflows.

Multi-Mode Laser Matrix for Complex Professional Scenarios

Sermoon P1 features a 22 + 7 + 1 multi-mode blue laser matrix, combined with an innovative four-lens NIR structured light system, enabling accurate scanning across a wide range of professional applications.

* Single-Line Blue Laser - Deep Hole Scanning
Designed for capturing 3D data in deep holes, narrow gaps, and recessed structures.
* 7 Parallel-Line Blue Laser - Fine Detail Scanning
Enables high-resolution surface capture for intricate features and complex geometries.
* 22 Cross-Line Blue Laser - Fast Large-Part Scanning
Optimized for high-speed capture of overall geometry and dimensions.
* NIR Markerless Scanning - Large Objects & Human Body
Allows fast, marker-free scanning of large objects and the human body, ideal for efficient medium-to-large-scale modeling.

Professional Accuracy You Can Rely On

With up to 0.02 mm accuracy, Sermoon P1 delivers stable, repeatable results suitable for professional reverse engineering, inspection, and design workflows.

High-Speed Data Transmission with Wi-Fi 7

Equipped with next-generation Wi-Fi 7, Sermoon P1 enables ultra-fast, low-latency data transmission when connected to a PC. Compare to Wifi 6 that gives you 9.6 Gbps, Wifi 7 tri-band connection give you 46 Gbps.

Large scan datasets can be transferred smoothly and efficiently, reducing waiting time during data processing, inspection, and design - and helping professionals move seamlessly from scanning to downstream applications.

Integrated, Portable Design for On-Site Reverse Engineering

Designed as a true all-in-one professional 3D scanner, Sermoon P1 features a compact, integrated form factor that allows users to work anytime, anywhere. You can switch seamlessly between Standalone, Wired PC, and Wireless PC modes - adapt easily to any scanning environment or workflow.

Without the need for external computing hardware, cables, or fixed workstations, professionals can easily carry Sermoon P1 to workshops, job sites, or field locations - making on-site reverse engineering and inspection faster, more flexible, and more efficient.

Sermoon P1 is Designed for Continuous Professional Use

With dual swappable batteries, fast charging, and an integrated all-in-one design, Sermoon P1 is built for long, uninterrupted professional scanning sessions, whether in the workshop or on site.

Seamless Integration into Professional Software Ecosystems

Sermoon P1 integrates smoothly with mainstream professional software for reverse engineering, inspection, and design, ensuring a seamless workflow from scanning to modeling and manufacturing.

Scan data can be easily imported into mainstream reverse engineering, inspection, and design software such as QuichSurface and Geomagic Design X, streamlining workflows.

Sermoon P1 is Now Available Worldwide

Sermoon P1 is now available globally, offering professionals a new level of freedom and efficiency in 3D scanning.

Sermoon P1 is built for professionals who demand industrial-level results - without industrial-level complexity.

Published Wednesday, February 18, 2026

Creality introduced the CFS-C, a four-spool multi-material add-on for K1 series printers that cuts filament to reduce waste. Prusa unveiled the CORE One L, a larger CoreXY system featuring the OpenPrintTag filament recognition system. Bambu Lab instituted stricter moderation policies on MakerWorld to curb low-effort AI-generated content, following similar moves by other platforms.

Creality CFS-C: multi-material upgrade for K1 series.

Creality has officially launched the CFS-C, an external 4-spool material station designed for the K1 and K1 Max. The unit features an active filament cutting mechanism that minimizes purge waste compared to traditional splicing systems.

What this means for you

The CFS-C is Creality's direct answer to Bambu Lab's AMS. By making it compatible with the existing K1 base, they are protecting their user base from migrating. The 'cut-and-retract' method vs. Bambu's 'cut-and-flush' is a key differentiator; if the CFS-C can reliably prove it uses less filament per swap, it becomes a major selling point for eco-conscious makers. It also signals that multi-material is now the baseline expectation for any flagship FDM printer in 2026.

attributes.body:
Creality launches filament recycling system for the desktop.

Filament Maker M1 & Shredder R1 could change the way filament is made at home.

Stay up to date with everything that is happening in the wonderful world of AM via our LinkedIn community.

Creality has launched a crowdfunding campaign for the Filament Maker M1 & Shredder R1 - a proprietary recycling system for 3D printing materials. Its goal is to process waste generated during printing into new filament. The project responds to the growing interest in sustainable production and in reducing material losses in 3D printing, particularly during the creation of multicolor models.

Established companies such as Creality primarily use crowdfunding as a marketing tool, and it is highly likely that they will commercialize the system. Understanding whether (or rather, how) the system will support filaments from other brands will be fascinating.

The system is intended to enable the use of leftover filaments, failed prints, and waste generated by AMS/CFS systems (so-called filament poo) to produce new consumable material. Such solutions have remained an ambitious goal for many startups for years; in most cases, their commercial implementations have failed.

The most common problems concerned the economics of the process and the quality of the obtained filament. Additionally, the entire process was very time-consuming, the entry threshold was high, and the final result was unsatisfactory. Ultimately, the total cost of home recycling exceeded the cost of a new spool of material, undermining the appeal of such a solution.

Therefore, the success of Creality's solution will depend on two key factors: an affordable system price and simplicity of everyday use. The process of processing plastics into filament form is technologically demanding, and even small parameter deviations may affect print stability.

The crowdfunding campaign will verify market interest in this type of solution and indicate whether users are ready to invest in local recycling of 3D printing materials. If the project proves technically and economically feasible, it may be a significant step toward a more circular model of material use in home 3D printing.
